narrator_001_once: <speak>Once, a long time ago, when I was a little girl, my grandmother told me a story. I have never forgotten it.</speak>
girl_001_scary: <speak>Yadda, tell me a scary one. A true one.</speak>
yadda_001_true: <speak>A true one?<break time="420ms"/> Nobody knows if this one is true. But everybody in Kuwait knows it.</speak>
yadda_002_sabahiya: <speak>It happened in Sabahiya, in nineteen ninety-seven. To a singer called Noura.</speak>
yadda_003_famous: <speak>In those days, Noura was the most famous tagaga in Kuwait. A wedding singer. She and her band of women, with their drums and their old songs, were booked months ahead, all over the Gulf.</speak>
yadda_004_phone: <speak>One quiet evening, the phone rang. A woman's voice. She said she was the mother of the bride.</speak>
mother_001_tomorrow: <speak>We are having a wedding tomorrow night, in Sabahiya. My daughter wants only you.</speak>
yadda_005_fortune: <speak>Five hundred dinars, in those days, was a fortune. So Noura said yes.</speak>
yadda_006_car: <speak>The next night, a car came for them. The driver never said one word.</speak>
yadda_007_dark: <speak>They drove past the last houses of Sabahiya, and kept going, into the dark.</speak>
yadda_008_house: <speak>Then, out of nowhere, a house. Huge, and blazing with light.</speak>
yadda_009_never_seen: <speak>Noura had sung in every big house in Kuwait. She had never seen this one.</speak>
yadda_010_gold: <speak>Inside, the women's hall was gold from the floor to the ceiling. Hundreds of guests in shining dresses. So much incense the air was blue. And at the far end, on a stage, the bride, under a heavy veil.</speak>
yadda_011_cold: <speak>The mother of the bride took Noura's hand. Her fingers were ice cold.</speak>
mother_003_play: <speak>Play. And do not stop until the bride has gone.</speak>
yadda_012_danced: <speak>So they played. And the guests danced.</speak>
yadda_013_one_person: <speak>Hundreds of hands, clapping on exactly the same beat. Like one person.</speak>
yadda_014_eyes: <speak>Nobody touched the food. Nobody spoke. And when the lights flickered, their eyes shone, like a cat's eyes in the dark.</speak>
yadda_015_youngest: <speak>The youngest girl in the band leaned close to Noura, still drumming.</speak>
yadda_016_hooves: <speak>Under the long dresses, where their feet should be, there were hooves. Some like a goat. Some like a donkey. Clicking on the marble, in time with the drums.</speak>
yadda_017_where: <speak>Run? Where to? Nobody knew where that house was.</speak>
noura_002_keep: <speak>Keep playing. Whatever you see, do not stop.</speak>
yadda_018_sounds: <speak>And under the music, they began to hear other sounds. Something braying behind the walls. Laughing that was not laughing. And voices singing along with Noura's songs, in a language none of them knew.</speak>
yadda_019_all_night: <speak>They played all night. Their hands cracked and bled on the drums. They smiled, and sang, and never looked down.</speak>
yadda_021_silent: <speak>Just before dawn, the mother of the bride raised her hand, and the hall went silent.</speak>
mother_004_enough: <speak>Enough. Thank you, Noura. You were everything they said.</speak>
yadda_022_paid: <speak>They were paid, exactly as promised. And they walked out into the grey morning, shaking, without a word.</speak>
yadda_023_man: <speak>Outside, a man was standing in the sand, staring at them.</speak>
man_001_empty: <speak>What are you doing here? Nobody lives in this house. It has been empty for years.</speak>
yadda_025_ruin: <speak>The house was a ruin. Broken windows. Sand blowing through the doorway. The walls black from an old fire. No lights. No cars. No music.</speak>
yadda_026_hoofprints: <speak>Only their footprints in the sand. And all around them, hundreds of small hoofprints.</speak>
yadda_027_never: <speak>After that night, Noura never sang at a wedding again. People say she never told anyone why.</speak>
yadda_028_newspaper: <speak>A newspaper printed the story, without her name. And since then, it has been told a thousand ways.</speak>
yadda_029_nobody: <speak>Nobody ever proved it happened. And nobody ever proved it didn't.</speak>
yadda_030_listen: <speak>But listen to me, habibti. If a stranger ever calls you, and offers far too much to sing at a wedding you never heard of<break time="420ms"/></speak>
